newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm, gains seen short-lived.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm, gains seen short-lived.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended a touch firmer on Wednesday, rebounding after two days of losses.
But traders said turnover remained extremely sluggish and see no pick-up in activity over the short term.
The SBI index rose 0.22 percent or 2.88 points to 1,318.92. Overall five shares rose, 10 fell and 13 were untraded. Turnover fell to 59.2 million tolars from 91.3 million tolars.
"Market will move nowhere until fresh foreign capital enters the market or some new information becomes available," lamented Andrej Ciuha, a trader at brokerage Inter Timex.

In February the central bank blocked foreign buying, ordering international portfolio investors to open custody accounts at one of Slovenia's 14 fully licensed banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenia's securities.
Since then the blue-chip index has dropped over 20 percent, while average daily volume dwindled to a quarter of its previous size.

Traders expressed cautious optimism concerning future political development in the country, whose parliament is expected to vote next week on whether to ratify the association accord with the EU, signed in June last year.

The Constitutional Court is expected to decide on Thursday whether parliament needs to change the constitution in a way that would allow foreigners to own real estate before ratifying the association agreement with the European Union.
"A positive decision could boost prices over the short term, (but) I cannot imagine what would happen if the decision is negative," one trader said.
Petrol trader Petrol was the most actively traded share, easing 0.18 percent to 17,060 tolars on volume of 602 shares for total turnover of 10.3 million tolars.
Traders said Petrol remains one of most interesting shares on the bourse due to its business performance and strategic importance.

Shopping centre operator BTC was among the top gainers, jumping 5.46 percent to 14,790 tolars on volume of 418 shares. BTC rose on expectation it would soon finalise its global depository receipts (GDRs) issue.
Ordinary shares of bank Dolenjska Banka were the top gainers, jumping 6.90 percent to 15,500 tolars on volume of 300 shares.
"Dolenjska banka still plans to introduce a 15 percent foreign stake in the bank although it postponed the final decision on the issue last month, and that is fuelling gains," one trader said.
Brokerage Finmedia led the day's decliners, tumbling 8.88 percent to 12,210 tolars on volume of 211 shares.
Traders attributed the fall to concerns over the company's public relations policy as the firm has still not released 1996 business results.
